data.why: the repo ships real riper outputs (bands.xyz, output.txt, dos/pdos files) and CIFs under band_plotting_examples/, dos_plotting_examples/ and orthogonalization_example/ that exactly match what the Bands_Plot, DOS_Plot, Output_Parser, Convert_other_formats_to_RIPER and Orthogonalizer pages expect to upload

goals: Upload a CIF/XYZ/POSCAR structure and generate a RIPER `control` input file (coordinates in Bohr, $cell, $periodic, $kpoints blocks) via the Convert_other_formats_to_RIPER page
Generate a high-symmetry k-point path ($kpoints / kptlines block) for a periodic structure on the Band_Structure_Path page
Plot a band structure from a riper `bands.xyz`/`bands_proj.xyz` file, set the Fermi/VBM energy reference, and detect the band gap on the Bands_Plot page
Plot total and projected (element/atom/shell) density of states from riper `dos`/`pdos_*` files, checking the Mulliken sum rule, on the DOS_Plot page
Parse a finished riper output file to extract Fermi level, VBM/CBM and band gap statistics on the Output_Parser page
Orthogonalize a non-orthogonal periodic cell (CIF) into an orthogonal supercell suitable for surface/slab RIPER calculations on the Orthogonalizer page

review.summary: This is a well-evidenced, correctly worded tree of the periodic-DFT input-prep and band/DOS-analysis workflow. Every screen I sampled matches its node, and the features are lift-able components cut at sensible sizes. It needs fixes before filing: the notes misdiagnose the output.txt Fermi-block failure and invent an Output Parser gap feature, and it omits the supercell builder plus README-stated scope (database import, RT-TDDFT input, spectra).
